$comment: Repository scope. Every tracked file is either digested by bundle/manifest.json or declared here with the reason it is not. tools/validate.py fails on any tracked path matching neither.
$why: On 2026-08-21 an entire second product — a systems engineering kit, with source, a package manifest and no lockfile or tests — was committed to this repository and CI stayed green. Nothing was wrong with CI. build-bundle.sh digests an explicit BUNDLE_FILES allowlist and validate.py globs only decisions/ and overlays/, so no guard in this repository has ever looked at the tree as a whole. A directory that nothing enumerates is a directory that nothing governs, and the standard that blocks a product repository for shipping source without a lockfile had done exactly that to itself. This file exists so that the next unenumerated directory fails a check instead of a review.

ungoverned.reason: The repository front door. Describes the standard; is not part of it. A consumer vendors the standard, never this.

The release history. Describes what changed between releases so a consumer can decide whether to re-sync; it is not content a consumer vendors, for the same reason README.md is not. A project keeps its own changelog.

The Apache License 2.0, verbatim (ADR 0037). At the root because that is where GitHub and every license scanner look. Not digested: vendored paths mirror source paths, and a digested LICENSE would land on a consumer's own root LICENSE. sync.sh copies it to bundle/LICENSE instead, and build-archive.sh ships it.
The Apache-2.0 attribution notice (ADR 0037). Not digested for the same reason as LICENSE, and copied to bundle/NOTICE by sync.sh.

The guide for a first outside adopter: which kind of use is which, and the measurements the open items wait on. Describes adopting the standard; is not part of it, for the same reason README.md is not.
Who maintains this repository and how it changes (ADR 0038). Governs the standard's source, not a consumer, so it is not vendored.
How to contribute to the standard itself (ADR 0038). Not vendored: a consumer's CONTRIBUTING.md is seeded from templates/contributor-START-HERE.md and is about that project.
How to report a vulnerability in the standard (ADR 0038). Governs this repository; a consumer keeps its own policy.
This repository's reviewer map (ADR 0038). A consumer's is seeded from templates/CODEOWNERS.
This repository's own issue forms (ADR 0038). A consumer's field-note form is seeded from templates/field-note-issue-form.yml.
The digest itself. A manifest cannot digest itself without changing the digest it just computed.
This file. Listed rather than special-cased, because a scope declaration that exempts itself by hiding in the code is the failure it exists to catch.
The standard's own gate, per ADR 0010. It runs the standard against itself and is not content a consumer vendors.
ADRs governing the standard. They are this repository's decision record, not text a consumer inherits — a consumer keeps its own decisions/.

This repository's open-items index. Same reason as decisions/*.md above: it is this repository's record of its own open items, not text a consumer inherits — a consumer gets templates/open-items.json and keeps its own. Ungoverned by the digest and not ungoverned by the build: tools/validate.py §17 checks it against every register it names, which is the point of it existing.
Distribution and validation machinery. tools/check-drift.sh is the exception and is bundled, because it runs in consumer CI and its drift must be detectable.
The standard's own validator. Verifies the source of truth against itself; deliberately not the same code as the consumer-facing check-drift.sh.
Generated from AGENTS.md by tools/render-adapters.sh, which CI re-runs and diffs. Digesting a generated file would pin a derivative of an input already under digest.
The engine conformance pack: fixtures and expected verdicts. Engines consume it to prove they implement the standard; product repositories do not vendor it.
The overlay index. Every overlay itself is digested by build-bundle.sh; this file only lists them.
Written into a consumer repository once by sync.sh and thereafter owned by that repository. Pinning it would make every consumer's local edits read as drift.

Written into a consumer repository once by sync.sh and thereafter owned by that repository, exactly as templates/project-CLAUDE.md is. Pinning it would make every consumer's own items read as drift, which is the one thing an index of items must never do.

Written into a consumer repository once by sync.sh as START-HERE.md and thereafter owned by that repository, exactly as templates/project-CLAUDE.md is. It ships with bracketed placeholders a project must replace — who reviews a note, who to ask when stuck — so pinning it would make every filled-in name read as drift, and an on-ramp still carrying [NAME] tells a new practitioner they were not expected.

Written into a consumer repository once by sync.sh as CONTRIBUTING.md and thereafter owned by that repository, exactly as templates/practitioner-START-HERE.md is. It ships with bracketed placeholders only the project can fill — its commands, its rules, who to ask — so pinning it would make every filled-in line read as drift. ADR 0035.

Seeded once into a consumer's .github/pull_request_template.md and thereafter owned by that repository. Its second section is the project's own checklist by construction, so the digest would pin the half a project has to replace. ADR 0035.

Seeded once into a consumer's .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ and thereafter owned by that repository. Its labels and assignee are per-project by construction, so the digest would pin the two fields a project has to change to make the browser path work at all.

Seeded once into a consumer's domain/field-notes/ and thereafter owned by that repository. It exists so the register is committable — git tracks files, not directories — and its links are relative to a layout the project may move.

Seeded once into a consumer's decisions/ and thereafter owned by that repository, exactly as templates/field-notes-README.md is. Its index by family and its list of unused numbers are the project's content by construction, so pinning it would make every row a project adds read as drift. ADR 0041.

Seeded once into a consumer's .github/CODEOWNERS and thereafter owned by that repository. It ships with @ORG/TEAM placeholders by construction, because a reviewer map naming teams that do not exist nominates nobody and fails silently; pinning it would make every project that filled in its real teams read as drift.
Excludes Python bytecode. Repository hygiene, not standard content; a consumer's ignore rules are its own.
